additionalCoursework:
Applicants are encouraged to acquire a broad undergraduate education, including coursework in the arts and humanities and in the behavioral and social sciences.

Here is more information about our required and recommended coursework: https://www.utoledo.edu/med/md/admissions/index.html

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The Admissions Office works in cooperation with the Office of Inclusion and Opportunity, the Office of Student Affairs, and other campus departments in the recruitment, selection, and retention of qualified students.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: A student may request a Leave of Absence (LOA) for one of several reasons including medical, academic, financial, personal, or administrative.  With the exception of a Medical Leave, a student must be in good academic standing to request a LOA.  All students approved, regardless of the type, must also request and be approved to return from the leave.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: The Office of Student Life recognizes over 50 student organizations on the Health Science Campus including specialty-based interest groups and several multicultural and service organizations. There are three national medical honor societies- Alpha Omega Alpha, The Gold Humanism Honor Society, and The Honor Society of Phi Kappha Phi.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The University of Toledo Health Science Campus is located on 475 acres in suburban south Toledo, approximately three miles south of the Main Campus. Toledo's many cultural attractions include the world famous Toledo Museum of Art, a symphony orchestra, opera company, and a zoological gardens.  Recreational activities include metro parks, boating, fishing, hiking, and cross-country skiing.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: On-campus housing is available on the main campus.  However, most students live in apartments located near the Health Science Campus.

medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture:
The campus culture at the University of Toledo College of Medicine and Life Sciences embodies a blend of academic excellence, collaboration, and a strong commitment to community involvement. Key elements of our culture include:

-Commitment to Community Engagement and Service
-Collaborative and Supportive Environment
-Focus on Innovation and Research
-Vibrant Student Life

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Yes. There is a written dress code policy.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: The Academic Enrichment Center (AEC) provides individual & group tutoring services for all medical students via an online scheduling process. http://www.utoledo.edu/med/depts/aec/
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: During the second semester of the first year.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Currently, information sessions regarding clinical rotations start in March of the second year. Required rotations start in the third year.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The preclinical basic science content is integrated into the following interdisciplinary instructional units: Genes, Genomes & Cell Biology, Hematology & Oncology, Immunity, Infection & Disease, Musculoskeletal, Neuroscience, Behavior, Cardiopulmonary, Renal, Gastrointestinal, and Reproduction. The curriculum is systems-based, integrating foundational science with clinical decision-making. An emphasis on clinical reasoning and clinical skills will span all four years with the utilization of more innovative educational methods and approaches. There will be a focus on Interprofessional education, patient safety, and career development. The third year of the curriculum is devoted to mandatory clerkships in internal medicine, surgery, pediatrics, obstetrics and gynecology, psychiatry, family medicine, and neurology, as well as a 4-week elective. The fourth year of elective clerkships consists of 44 weeks, including a basic science elective requirement and a required acting internship.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Major areas of grant funding include cardiovascular medicine and hypertension, cancer, neurosciences, and microbiology/immunology.
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: More information on our curriculum can be found at https://www.utoledo.edu/med/md/curriculum/
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: No. Optional research projects are available

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: The Medical University of Ohio and the University of Toledo merged on July 1, 2006, thus creating the third largest university in Ohio, which is now known as The University of Toledo. The health and research colleges located on the Health Science Campus include the College of Medicine and Life Science, the College of Nursing, and the College of Pharmacy along with The University of Toledo Medical Center.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
Our Mission: 
To improve health in the communities and region we serve by educating and training excellent clinicians and scientists, providing high-quality patient care and conducting nationally recognized research.

Our Vision:
The University of Toledo College of Medicine and Life Sciences is the leader in innovative education, transformative research and world-class clinical care.

Our Values:
The College of Medicine and Life Science’s core values include collaboration, discovery, intellectual diversity, life-long learning, professionalism and service.
medSchoolInformation.programAbout:
The BACC2MD program is The University of Toledo's early medical school pathway program offered to high-metric high school students pursuing a major from a participating college at UToledo. Eligible students have the opportunity for a guaranteed interview with the MD program at UToledo.

This is a sequential degree program. Students who are conditionally accepted to the MD program first complete the undergraduate degree, followed by the MD at UToledo College of Medicine and Life Sciences (COMLS)

Program Restrictions:
- Other Restrictions: The program is an internal (University of Toledo) early assurance program. Eligible students must be identified by the UToledo Pre-Health Advising Office to qualify for a junior year MD program interview. Students must be U.S. citizens or permanent residents at the time of application. 
- Applicants applying through this program are NOT permitted to apply to other schools
- Pre-approval required

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: Committee letters are accepted and meet the 3-letter requirements.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
All letters of recommendation must be submitted through AMCAS. Letters sent directly to the College of Medicine and Life Sciences will not be reviewed or considered.

We do not have specific requirements regarding who your letters must be from. Applicants may submit a premedical advisory committee letter, a letter packet, or individual letters. While many applicants choose to include letters from faculty members who have taught them, this is not required. Letters may come from faculty or from individuals who can speak to your experiences since graduation, such as a supervisor, employer, or volunteer coordinator.

The most important consideration is that your letters come from individuals who know you well and can meaningfully speak to your personal qualities, motivation, professionalism, and academic or professional abilities. Letters from friends, family members, or family friends are not appropriate and will not be considered.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: For the 2026-2027 interview cycle, all of our interviews will be conducted as synchronous, virtual Multiple Mini Interviews (MMI). The interview experience will consist of informal gatherings with medical students from our COMLS Ambassadors, as well as virtual tours and presentations from other campus administrators. (Most of these experiences will occur outside of the interview day.) The interview visit day will include a presentation about our interview format and a 2-hour MMI session with eight interviewees. If you're invited for an interview, the email we send you will contain additional information, including technical requirements and access to the web-based platform.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Multiple Mini Interview (MMI) format with faculty, senior staff, residents, community members and medical students.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: Synchronous, online MMI will be conducted for all interviews during the 2026-2027 admissions cycle.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Financial aid is awarded on the basis of demonstrated financial need according to federal methodology. Applicants for financial aid must file the FAFSA. Several full tuition Presidential Scholarships are available, as well as a number of both merit and need-based scholarships. Some students are employed during the academic year in the Federal Work-Study Program. Employment opportunities in research, community health and family practice are also provided through the summer preceptorship programs. Here is more information regarding Financial Aid: https://www.utoledo.edu/financialaid/hsc/

medSchoolPrograms.info:
The MSBS in Medical Sciences Degree (MSBS-MS) is a 1-year postbacc graduate program designed to enhance the academic credentials of applicants who have completed all prerequisites for medical school.  MSBS-MS students in good academic standing and with an MCAT of 496 or above are eligible to be interviewed at UTCOMLS Medical School.
 
The curriculum emphasizes an organ systems approach where clinical and graduate faculty train students in the pathophysiology of disease and pharmacological interventions. The graduate-level courses in our curriculum incorporate materials taught to medical students, thus setting a strong foundation for the MD curriculum. The MSBS-MS program also allows students to achieve meaningful clinical and/or basic science research experience. UToledo’s basic and clinical science faculty mentor students in a year-round Scholarly Project, allowing students to expand their view on experimental sciences while adding a strong component to their academic credentials.

JD/MD, MD/Ph.D, MD/MSBS - Doctor of Medicine and Master of Science in Biomedical Sciences
MD/MPH, MD/MBA.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
UToledo COMLS requires the following prerequisite coursework: 
- One semester of Biochemistry 
- One year of Biological Sciences 
- One year of Organic Chemistry with Labs
- One year of Physics

Frequently Asked Questions: 
Is AP (Advanced Placement) credit accepted?
Yes. It must be shown on a college transcript as verified by AMCAS.

Is online coursework accepted in fulfillment of prerequisites?
Yes, with the exception of science lab courses.

Is community college coursework accepted in fulfillment of prerequisites?
Yes. It must be shown on a college transcript as verified by AMCAS.
medSchoolSelection.medSchoolMediaSites: Each class has there own Facebook page, accessed by invitation-only.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: No limit. However, competitive applicants generally have prerequisites completed  as part of an undergraduate degree, graduate degree, or postbaccalaureate program within 5 years prior to application.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors:
UToledo COMLS holistically reviews applicants' experiences, attributes, and academic qualifications in order to select individuals who align with our mission. We seek candidates who will grow into lifelong learners and essential contributors to the medical community—as students, practitioners, educators, and researchers.

Key attributes we value include a commitment to community service, academic excellence, professionalism, integrity, and ethics. We also prioritize strong interpersonal, social, and communication skills, teamwork, clinical experience, research involvement, leadership, resilience, adaptability, reliability, and dependability.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: While we have no specific requirements related to premedical shadowing, we recommend shadowing and other healthcare related experiences where you can can demonstrate meaningful learning and growth as opposed to merely a large quantity of activities.
